attribution.note: Marcus's own post, co-signed with Elliot Murphy. The sentence is the authors' own description of DALL-E, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The prompt condition (blue cube on top of red) is kept. The wording is probabilistic ('may', 'as likely as not'), so under the policy this is a hedged frequency description and is not scored. The draft's 'about as often as not' also drops the 'may produce both' qualifier.

contract.note: The contract correctly applies the probabilistic-language exclusion and does not invent a frequency threshold.

reviews.rationale: The statement uses probabilistic wording ('may', 'as likely as not') about how often DALL-E reverses the cubes. The policy excludes probabilistic or possibility language from scoring. The packet holds no evidence, which is consistent with the exclusion.

attribution.note: Marcus's own post, co-signed with Elliot Murphy. The words are the authors' own assertion.

semantics.note: Faithful: the LLM approach ignores the linguistics work on models of meaning and the cognitive-psychology work (e.g. Kintsch) on how those models are derived. It is a firm, general characterisation of a research approach.

contract.note: Under the contradiction condition, a single niche preprint can refute a generic claim about 'the approach', which stretches the reading against the speaker. It also widens 'this literature' beyond models of meaning and comprehension (Kintsch-style) to cover neuroscience theory of predictive coding. An ordinary reader would take the claim to be about the dominant LLM approach.

evidence.note: This genuine 2021 preprint extends BERT using predictive-coding theory. Predictive coding is a theory of prediction, not the meaning-model or Kintsch comprehension literature named, and one niche variant does not show that the mainstream approach engaged with that literature.

reviews.rationale: Read fairly, the claim is about the mainstream LLM approach and the meaning and comprehension literature. e4 is one preprint drawing on predictive coding, which is not clearly 'this literature' and does not describe the dominant approach. No item establishes support, and the contract's single-counterexample test is unfair, so the packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own post, co-signed with Elliot Murphy. The words are the authors' own.

semantics.note: The draft narrows 'any of that' to building cognitive models. The context also bundles grasping intent, drawing inferences and feeling emotion. 'Don't really show up' is figurative and sets no threshold.

contract.note: The contract reasonably declines to impose a threshold. The bundled capacities and the qualifier 'really' leave no unique test, so any score would depend on a reading the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: A dated 2021 NeurIPS paper on neuro-symbolic gains in story coherence. It is relevant functional work but does not address the bundled human capacities in the claim.

reviews.rationale: The statement is a broad, figurative characterisation ('don't really show up for any of that') covering several distinct cognitive capacities, with no operational threshold. It cannot be scored without adding criteria the speaker did not supply. e3 is context only.

attribution.note: The statement is in a footnote of Marcus's post, co-signed with Elliot Murphy. Piantadosi is cited only as the view being rebutted; the claim is the authors' own.

semantics.note: Scope is limited to the contemporary sentence-clustering neural systems such as GPT-3. Both asserted absences (reference; ties to dynamically updated cognitive models) are kept. 'Pretty' is rhetorical.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: reference to the external world and updatable world models, assessed as a snapshot on the post date. Weak evidence such as selected prompt failures or discourse tracking is excluded in both directions.

evidence.note: A 2020 position paper arguing that systems trained only on form cannot learn meaning. It is a theoretical argument consistent with the claim, not a measurement of the systems current on 2022-06-22.
A 2024 philosophical counterargument on reference, published before the evaluation date. It explicitly disclaims being a decisive argument and measures no in-scope system.

reviews.rationale: Both items are theoretical arguments, one on each side. Neither establishes, for the systems current in mid-2022, that both external-world reference and ties to updated world models were present or absent. The packet notes that the empirical grounding paper it wanted could not be read. The evidence does not settle the claim.
